provided by a third-party vendor, then automatically routed each payment via one or more

intermediary banks. In some instances, Bank of America’s systems were unable to map the routing

automatically, and routing was input manually by a bank employee. Bank of America’s customers

could also manually identify banks (e.g., intermediary banks) when inputting payment details.

Once payment details were generated, they were screened by Bank of America for compliance with

OFAC-administered sanctions.

In March 2022, following the imposition of sanctions in connection with Russia’s February 2022

invasion of Ukraine, Bank of America became aware that the routing directory included banks that

had been blocked by OFAC pursuant to the Russian Harmful Foreign Activities Sanctions

Regulations (“RuHSR”), 31 C.F.R. part 587, and that although it was screening these payments,

including the details of the banks involved in the payments, for compliance with OFAC-administered sanctions, it was nevertheless processing certain payments to or through blocked

banks. This generally occurred because:

1. The payments were processed shortly after the relevant bank was blocked by OFAC and

before Bank of America updated its sanctions screening filter to reflect the bank’s

blocked status;

2. Due to human error, the payments were identified as false positives and approved for

processing by analysts in the sanctions screening or payments teams; or

3. D espite alerting in Bank of America’s system, the payments were released automatically

after the issue was initially identified, in February 2024, Bank of America fully implemented

# 445. What are my compliance obligations with respect to E.O. 13694, as amended?
As a general matter, U.S. persons, including firms that facilitate or engage in online commerce, are responsible for ensuring that they do not engage in unauthorized transactions or dealings with persons named on any of OFAC’s sanctions lists or operate in jurisdictions targeted by comprehensive sanctions programs. Such persons, including technology companies, should develop a tailored, risk-based compliance program, which may include sanctions list screening or other appropriate measures.

The names of, and identifying information for, all individuals and entities included on OFAC’s sanctions lists may be located via OFAC’s free, online search engine at the following URL: http://sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov. In addition, OFAC offers text and PDF versions of these lists for manual review and a number of data file versions of its lists that are designed to facilitate automated screening.
